paper.title_en: Sub-Riemannian lift advantage in quantum control
paper.abstract_en: We present an extended-algebra (EA) control workflow for fixed-horizon, bounded-amplitude quantum control. The method optimizes a state-transfer trajectory in a polynomial EA, projects the optimized lifted trajectory to native physical controls using a budgeted dictionary of product-formula approximants, and then refines the resulting waveform on the original idealized physical model with gradient ascent pulse engineering (GRAPE). The sub-Riemannian gradient ascent pulse engineering (SR-GRAPE) method and the direct-GRAPE baseline use the same physical Hamiltonian, amplitude bounds, time horizon, discretization, and terminal physical optimizer; the difference is the initialization supplied to the final physical-space optimization. For Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) preparation with Ising-coupled qubits and local <math><mrow><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.28em"/><mi>and</mi><mspace width="0.28em"/><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> drives, SR-GRAPE changes which basin is reached. In the five-qubit state-growing benchmark, SR-GRAPE reaches <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">F</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow></math> in <math><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> trials with mean fidelity 0.9917, whereas direct physical-space GRAPE from random feasible initialization remains near the <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">F</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow></math> GHZ plateau in all 25 trials. Six-qubit state-growing also gives <math><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> successes at <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">F</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow></math>, while direct GRAPE remains at mean fidelity 0.4998 with <math><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> successes. In a seven-qubit resource-extended setting with <math><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mo movablelimits="true" form="prefix">max</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>, SR-GRAPE again reaches <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">F</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow></math> in <math><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> seeds with mean fidelity 0.9901, whereas the corresponding direct-GRAPE baseline remains at mean fidelity 0.5000 with <math><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> successes. For the GHZ task, <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">F</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow></math> certifies genuine multipartite entanglement; the <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">F</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow></math> plateau does not cross this witness threshold.
